finding.headline: You can count on $29,000 a year: $22,000 for basics and $7,000 for the rest.
details: Your basics cost about $22,000 a year.
Your spending goal is $22,000 a year, and it lasts in 100 of 100 scenarios, so the goal works.

assumptions: All figures are in today's dollars: what money buys now, not the larger sums prices will reach.

Savings grow on average 5.0% a year above inflation in stocks and 1.8% in bonds, with good and bad years. The plan tests many possible market paths. These are planning figures, not a forecast. They are fixed, so every plan is tested on the same markets; to see a bad stretch, try a What If such as markets fall 30%.
You already get Social Security (from 70): the plan uses the $25,600 a year you gave.
After the first death (at the shorter life expectancy), Social Security falls to the larger of your two benefits, about $17,100 a year, and spending falls to 75% of what the two of you spend.

Tax uses the 2027 federal brackets, the standard deduction and your state's rates. In retirement the plan counts 85% of Social Security as taxable, the most the law allows, so the tax may be a little high.
The plan runs to age 99. There is about a 1 in 4 chance that one of you will live that long (US life table, SOA 2024). People with more money tend to live longer than that table says.
